chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Sukayn ibn 'Ammar, from Fudayl al-Rassan, from Farwa, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'Order your people to begin with salt and end with it, or else let them not blame anyone but themselves.'

key_terms.فَلَا يَلُومُوا إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: Let them not blame except themselves

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of eating salt at the beginning and end of a meal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual and physical merits of salt, linking dietary habits to divine instruction given to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). The phrase 'or else let them not blame anyone but themselves' suggests that while the practice is highly recommended and beneficial, its omission carries personal consequence rather than constituting a strict legal fault, emphasizing its status as a virtuous tradition (sunnah) in Shia scholarly tradition.
